text:
raja: Hey all  new hire here. I'm on hotel Wi-Fi with a captive portal. WireGuard shows as connected on my Ubuntu laptop but I can't reach internal console (console.redwood) from terminal apps. Browser on the laptop (after signing into the portal) can load the UI intermittently, but `curl` and `ssh` fail with timeouts or TLS errors. Anybody seen captive-portal + split-tunnel weirdness?
it-support: Welcome! Captive portals + hotel NATs are notorious. Can you paste `wg show`, `ip route`, and `resolvectl status` (or /etc/resolv.conf) output? Also try `curl -v https://console.redwood` so we see where it stalls.
raja: wg shows handshake ok, AllowedIPs includes 10.240.0.0/16; `ip route` has default via wlan0 and a route to 10.240.0.0/16 via wg0. `resolvectl` shows VPN DNS 10.240.1.2 but resolution sometimes returns the portal's captive IP. curl -v hangs at TLS handshake.
nikhil: Two likely causes: 1) the hotel's NAT/CGNAT rewrites DNS or intercepts HTTP(S) before you auth, 2) packets to internal IPs are hitting the hotel's gateway in a way that breaks path MTU or drops ICMP, causing TLS stalls. Quick checks: `traceroute -n 10.240.2.10` and `sudo sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter` please.
raja: traceroute to 10.240.2.10 hits wg0 then drops at our egress cloud hop (so path seems OK). rp_filter is 1.
it-support: rp_filter=1 can drop packets when using policy routing or marked routing. Also hotel networks sometimes block UDP->UDP reflections which can break WireGuard's encapsulation path for return traffic in tricky NATs. Two pragmatic workarounds: 1) use phone hotspot, 2) use bastion SOCKS proxy, 3) policy-route internal CIDRs explicitly via wg0 with a fwmark so the kernel doesn't try to send through wlan0.
nikhil: If you're comfortable, try this sequence (as root) to mark traffic destined to the VPC and route it via wg0 table:```bash
# mark packets destined for internal VPC
sudo iptables -t mangle -N REDWOOD_MARKER || true
sudo iptables -t mangle -F REDWOOD_MARKER
sudo iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -d 10.240.0.0/16 -j MARK --set-mark 1
# create policy routing table 200 -> use wg0
echo "200 redwood" | sudo tee -a /etc/iproute2/rt_tables
sudo ip rule add fwmark 1 lookup redwood
sudo ip route add default dev wg0 table redwood
# disable strict reverse path filter to allow asymmetric routing
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0
```
nikhil: This forces kernel to lookup table 'redwood' for marked packets so they go out wg0 directly. It often helps when hotel NATs confuse source interface selection.
raja: Trying now... (runs commands)
raja: After adding the iptables/ip rule trick `curl -v https://10.240.2.10:8443` now returns TLS cert chain, and `ssh -J raja@bastion.redwood internal-host` connects. :tada:
ops: Nice work! Two safety notes: 1) the echo to /etc/iproute2/rt_tables appends every time you run the script; edit the file idempotently in your onboarding note, 2) if you reboot the wg0 interface name changes or IP changes, you may need to re-run or add a small wg-quick pre-up script. We have a snippet in infra docs.
raja: Good call, I'll make it a small script in ~/bin/wg-hotel-fix and add a check so it doesn't duplicate the rt_tables entry.
it-support: If anyone else hits this, temporary alternatives: sign into the captive portal on host machine before starting WireGuard, or tether to phone. The policy-routing works when hotel path is the root cause.
infra-bot: Docs: https://confluence.redwood/infra/hotel-captive-vpn-policy-routing (add the policy-routing snippet, MTU hints, and a note about rp_filter) :white_check_mark:
raja: Thanks so much everyone! I'll paste the script and the minimal logs into the #new-hires checklist so future travelers aren't stuck.
nikhil: Welcome aboard and congrats on day 1 :party:
